points.point: Three permitted relationships; single (limited) agency requires a written agreement signed before brokerage activity
Single agents may cooperate with other brokers but may not create subagents
Broker is presumed a transaction-broker absent a written single-agency agreement
Dual agency is prohibited even with written consent
Customers vs. clients; ministerial tasks for a customer create no relationship
Written relationship disclosure is due before eliciting or discussing confidential information
Seller's agent working with a buyer must disclose in writing that it is the seller's agent, its tasks, and buyer's non-liability
Disclosure made in the engagement contract or a Brokerage Disclosure form; acknowledgment is not a contract; record a refusal to sign
Definitions of Working Relationships form is not by itself a disclosure; give the definition when asked about a relationship the firm doesn't offer
Working with both sides: TB for both, TB plus customer, or single agent plus customer
Change of Status form due no later than when the party signs the contract; agency-only box; reverts after the transaction
Designated brokerage: relationship only with the designated broker; opposite-side designated agents aren't dual agency; no imputed knowledge
Teams: every member designated in the same capacity and named in the listing
Employing broker: written office policy on relationships, continued supervision and firm liability; clients not vicariously liable
Relationship ends at earliest of expiration, termination or one year if not completed
After termination: account for money/property; single agent keeps requested confidences
Single agent duties: loyalty, present all offers even under contract, need not seek more offers while under contract
Transaction-broker duties focus on process (keep parties informed, present offers, help close); no advocacy
Seller's agent confidential information (will accept less, motivation, terms) needs informed consent
Transaction-broker confidentiality requires informed consent of all parties
Seller's agent must disclose known adverse material facts to buyers, even against seller's instructions
Actual-knowledge trigger; no duty to inspect or verify
Buyer's agent must disclose buyer's financial inability to perform and occupancy intent to seller
Psychologically impacted property: not material; may not disclose without client consent
Not breaches: showing other properties, competing buyers on the same property
Paying a broker doesn't create agency; disclose who pays; multi-party pay needs written consent
Buyer's agent needs buyer's written approval before seeking pay from seller's compensation
Seller/landlord listing must be in writing before services
Every listing needs a definite termination date
No relationship box checked = transaction-brokerage
Compensation is not set by law and is negotiable
Right-to-buy: buyer owes unpaid balance only if disclosed in writing before signing the purchase contract
Holdover clause covers only prospects named in writing during the listing term
Residential engagement contracts can't run with the land, be assigned without agreement, or create a lien (void; deceptive trade practice)
Licensee acting for own account must disclose license status in writing; disclose conflicts
Account requirements: separate, insured Colorado depository, titled trust/escrow, in firm's name
Funds available immediately without penalty; no CDs absent written agreement
A firm may have any number of trust accounts, including zero
Property management: separate accounts for rents and security deposits
Interest doesn't belong to the firm absent written agreement
Earnest money/other funds: deposit within 3 business days of receipt or mutual execution, whichever is later
Property management funds: 5 business days after receipt or lease execution, whichever is later
Promissory note as earnest money: notify seller and deliver note if unpaid
Releases: disburse as parties direct; one party's written authorization suffices; no hold-harmless release
Disputes: follow the contract (hold, interplead, return after notice)
Commingling vs. conversion; exceptions for bank charges and recorded advances
Earned fees must be withdrawn monthly
Security deposit transfer on management change: disclose within 30 days, transfer within 60
Journal, beneficiary ledgers with no negative balance, monthly three-way reconciliation
Owner reports due within 30 days after month-end if agreement is silent
Journal is chronological; ledger per beneficiary with no negative balance
Monthly three-way reconciliation report
Trust records also include bank statements, deposit agreements and written accounting control policies
Transaction file per Commission checklist; emails/texts recommended, not required
Items not required after closing (loan applications, title commitments, public records)
Keep records 4 years from closing
If no closing, 4 years from listing expiration
Broker stays responsible for files after changing firms
Closing responsibility; a substitute broker may attend and shares responsibility
Electronic records must be retrievable; a technical failure is no excuse
Records must be produced for the Commission or any principal party
Failing to respond to a complaint or audit by the deadline is itself grounds for discipline
Employing broker duties include a written PII-disposal policy and supervising staff
Division investigates; Commission decides
Audit selection: random, stipulation, or complaint-driven
Others' money held in non-brokerage activities belongs in a trust account
Common findings: commingling cushion
Common findings: negative ledger shows conversion
Earnest money held by a firm: 3 business days
Complaint jurisdiction: contract disputes and money claims are civil matters
Must respond in writing by the deadline; failure is a separate violation
Complaints and investigations closed; stipulations and final orders public
Letter of admonition: demand formal proceedings within 20 days
Formal discipline: fine up to $2,500 per offense
Revocation: no new application considered for one year
ALJ conducts the hearing
Court of Appeals reviews Commission orders
No recovery fund since 2005; E&O instead

Earnest money releases and disputes

Security deposit transfer between firms

Trust records and retention (L3+L4)
Retention period from closing / listing expiration

Letter of admonition
Revocation and appeal
